**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make body-only dispositions independently parseable**

For summary-only review findings, an issue comment has no parent thread or review binding, yet this format records only a bar marker and disposition verb—nothing identifies the originating body item or commit. The supplied fixture demonstrates the failure: comments `5645760733` and `5645946537` batch findings from multiple heads, open with headings rather than the required bold marker, and contain mixed per-row bar values. An implementation following this contract must therefore either infer associations from prose (contradicting the plan's recorded-field invariant) or report "manual tally required", so it cannot derive the promised per-round cure-worthy counts or terminal-zero verdict from this fixture. Require a machine-readable finding/round reference for each body-only disposition and make the fixture conform to that grammar.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: todo 1's parser is built from this paragraph, and as written it could not bind a body-only disposition to its round or item without reading prose — the invariant the node forbids breaking). The observation is right on both counts: the format named no reference for body-only dispositions, and the fixture's two reconciliation comments batch several heads under prose headings. Cured in `SHA:84dd6291b` for the part in this pull request's scope: the paragraph now requires a body-only disposition to be an issue comment with one line per finding — the marker, the reference `head SHA:<sha> · <path>:<line>` (the review body's own anchor), the disposition sentence — and says that a comment without the reference, or batched under headings, reads as "manual tally required" for those items. The remedy's second half — making the fixture conform — is out of scope by the declaration (the fixture is a recording, not edited); instead the README names those two comments as the corpus's manual-tally case, which criterion 5 needs covered anyway, and the thread replies as its marked case. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

The recorded replies at `pr-135-harvest.json:552`, `:591`, and `:630` begin `Cured in `SHA:...`` with the SHA as an inline Markdown code span, not the literal `Cured in SHA:<sha>` form stated here. Because this fixture is the corpus the next parser consumes, the grammar needs to say whether code-wrapped SHA tokens are valid.

This issue also appears on line 516 of the same file.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: the parser reads this grammar and the corpus it must accept uses the code span). Cured in `SHA:84dd6291b`: the paragraph now says the SHA token is the `SHA:` prefix and seven to forty hex characters, bare or inside a code span, both valid. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

Every connection here is capped with `first: 50`, but the query selects no `pageInfo`/`endCursor` and provides no `after`-cursor procedure. A larger PR will therefore be silently truncated (including nested thread comments), despite the next paragraph saying it can be paged and the tally contract requiring pagination to exhaustion. Add the actual pagination shape/procedure rather than only mentioning cursors.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong one: a reader re-recording a larger pull request with this query would get a silently truncated fixture and trust it). Cured in `SHA:84dd6291b`: every connection in the query now selects `pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }`, and the README states the procedure — while any `hasNextPage` is true, re-query that connection with `after: "<endCursor>"` and concatenate its `nodes`, the nested thread `comments` connection included, before unwrapping; a truncated recording is not a fixture. Evidence class READ.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add an item key to body-only disposition references**

When a review body contains two distinct findings at the same path and line—the case criterion 5 explicitly requires—or a body item duplicates an inline thread at that anchor, `head SHA + path:line` is identical for multiple logical items. The tally therefore cannot reliably determine which item an over-/below-bar line dispositions, which can mis-deduplicate the cure-worthy count or produce a false terminal-zero verdict. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the new reference adds only the head and anchor, not a stable finding ordinal, review ID, or substance key.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: the parser is built from this grammar, and head plus anchor collides on exactly the two-findings-at-one-anchor case criterion 5 requires). Cured in `SHA:db67da4d5`: the reference is now `head SHA:<sha> · <path>:<line> · <item>`, where the item key is a Codex item's bold heading, a Copilot suppressed item's ordinal in its block (`item 3 of 6`), or `thread <id>` when the body item restates an inline thread at that anchor and is counted once. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

The fixture does not exercise the claimed Codex review-body parser path: every Codex `reviews.nodes[].body` contains only the standard review boilerplate, while all badge-and-heading findings are first comments under `reviewThreads`. An implementation can therefore completely fail to parse summary-only Codex body findings while still passing this purported end-to-end corpus; add an actual Codex body-only finding fixture or remove this coverage claim and cover the shape separately.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong one: a reader trusting the coverage claim would believe the Codex body-only path exercised). Verified against the JSON: five Codex review bodies, none carrying a badge item; every Codex finding on #135 is a thread. The README's claim was mine and untested. Cured in `SHA:db67da4d5` for the in-scope half: the README now says there is no Codex body-only item in this corpus and that the shape takes a fixture of its own at todo 1. Adding a second recorded fixture here is outside the declared scope (the fixture is one recording of #135); it is named for todo 1, which consumes the fixtures. Evidence class READ.

In the fixture-capture path this removes the only machine-readable evidence that each connection was exhausted, so a truncated capture has the same accepted shape despite the later requirement that truncation be rejected; retain the captured `pageInfo` values or document and enforce validation before normalization.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong one: the provenance claim said the file came from a query the file did not match). Cured in `SHA:db67da4d5`: the fixture is re-recorded from the merged, unchanging #135 with `pageInfo` selected on every connection — the same 7/17/26/10 counts, twenty-one `pageInfo` objects, every `hasNextPage` false — so the README's query and the file agree and exhaustion is recorded in the file rather than asserted. Evidence class RUN (the re-recording) and READ.

Describing all ten as below-bar/terminal-success contradicts the tally semantics and the following sentence.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong one: a reader of the README, and todo 1's test, would assert terminal success from a corpus the contract reads as manual). Correct, and the same finding as the Codex thread at this anchor (counted once). Cured in `SHA:a1ec078e2`: the README now says the final head's two thread findings carry marked below-bar replies while its eight suppressed items are dispositioned only inside the batched comment `5645946537`, so the machine reading is "manual tally required" for those eight, not terminal success; a fixture test asserts the manual verdict. **In scope, over-bar** (prong one: the provenance claim did not match the file). **In scope, over-bar** (prong one: the README understated the corpus's manual-tally cases). **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require exactly one unambiguous bar marker**

When a disposition opens with text such as `**Not over-bar**` or `**Below-bar, not over-bar**`, the specified case-insensitive containment test accepts an unintended or conflicting marker, so the tally can classify the finding incorrectly and alter the terminal-zero or step-back verdict. Define a closed grammar that requires exactly one bar token rather than accepting any bold span containing either substring.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: a containment test would let `**Not over-bar**` count as over-bar and move the verdict). Cured in `SHA:a1ec078e2`: the marker is a bold span whose text contains exactly one of the tokens `over-bar` or `below-bar` and no other bar token; `**Not over-bar**` and `**Below-bar, not over-bar**` read as no marker. Checked against the corpus: all seventeen recorded replies still satisfy the closed grammar. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the originating review ID in body-item references**

When the same reviewer submits two reviews against one head—for example, after a review is re-requested without a push—the head and anchor remain identical, while `item 3 of 6` is only unique within each Copilot block and a Codex heading can recur. The parser therefore cannot tell which review-body item the disposition targets. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the added item key is scoped only to its review body while the reference still omits that body's review ID; include the review ID or another globally stable item identifier.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: two reviews by one reviewer on one head — a re-request without a push, which this very pull request has done — leave head plus anchor plus ordinal ambiguous). Cured in `SHA:a1ec078e2`: the reference is `head SHA:<sha> · review <id> · <path>:<line> · <item>`, the review's own id first. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

When todo 1 consumes this corpus, the final head's eight suppressed body findings cannot produce a machine-derived cure-worthy zero: this README now explicitly classifies their disposition comments as the `manual tally required` case at lines 141–143. Fresh evidence in this revision is that acknowledgement, which directly contradicts the terminal-success claim here and could lead the fixture test to assert a verdict the documented parser must refuse; either add parseable per-item dispositions or describe the expected result as manual.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar**, the same finding as the Copilot thread at this anchor (counted once). Cured in `SHA:a1ec078e2` as described there: the final head's machine reading is manual for its eight suppressed items; the terminal-success reading is the seat's human tally on the PR, and the fixture test asserts the manual verdict. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

The recorded seat replies end their signature as `— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director`, but the existing self-reply predicate requires the final line to end exactly in `(<six lowercase hex>)` (`agent-tools/src/pr-watch/reviewer-legs.ts:125-130`). Consequently these 17 replies are not recognised as signed self-replies and will not be excluded from the raised count/quiet-window as this fixture and the README claim. Either record the canonical bare-prefix signature or explicitly extend the parser and its tests to accept this exact role suffix while preserving the recorded corpus.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: the README claimed the replies are excluded as signed self-replies, and under the ratified predicate they are not). Verified: all seventeen end `— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director`, and `SIGNATURE_SUFFIX` requires the line to end with the six-hex prefix. Cured in `SHA:a1ec078e2` for what this pull request owns: the format paragraph names the signature as `reviewer-legs.ts` defines it (final line ends with the prefix, nothing after), the README states that every recorded reply carries the role suffix and therefore reads as NOT signed under the current code, and the node's ledger records the pickup question for todo 1 — widen the predicate by dated amendment or treat this corpus's replies as unsigned. The recording is not edited (it is a recording) and the parser is todo 1's, so neither of the thread's two alternatives is taken here. Evidence class READ.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define a marker grammar that rejects negation**

When the implementer follows the stated containment test, `**Not over-bar**` contains exactly one recognised token and therefore classifies as over-bar, directly contradicting the next sentence. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the replacement grammar still defines validity through substring containment while using this negative form as a rejection example; a parser following the former can change cure-worthy counts and the terminal verdict. Define a genuinely closed accepted pattern rather than relying on unspecified detection of negation. [.agent/rules/agent-experience-review-lens.mdL18-L21](https://github.com/EngraphCode/open-curriculum-ecosystem/blob/a1ec078e24c32c398ff3f2ac70e586c93f8e2d55/.agent/rules/agent-experience-review-lens.md#L18-L21)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: a parser built from a containment test would count a negated span). The same finding as the Copilot thread at this anchor (counted once). Cured in `SHA:33cca25bc`: the grammar is an accepted pattern, not a containment test — the span's ENTIRE text is an optional `In scope, ` / `Out of scope, ` prefix, then exactly `Over-bar` or `Below-bar`, then an optional ` on prong one` / ` on prong two`, then an optional full stop, and nothing else; `**Not over-bar**` and any span with other words read as no marker. Checked with `jq`: the corpus's seventeen spans are `Over-bar` (11), `Below-bar` (3), `Over-bar on prong one`, `Over-bar on prong two`, `Over-bar on prong two.` — all match. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

If todo 1 follows this text, `pr-tally` and `pr-watch` will disagree about whether the same reply is self-authored, allowing the tally to count a disposition as a raised finding and move its quiet-window anchor; document the predicate's optional `-hex3` arm or change both surfaces together. [.agent/rules/documentation-hygiene.mdL11-L15](https://github.com/EngraphCode/open-curriculum-ecosystem/blob/a1ec078e24c32c398ff3f2ac70e586c93f8e2d55/.agent/rules/documentation-hygiene.md#L11-L15)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The same finding as the Copilot thread at this anchor (counted once). Cured in `SHA:33cca25bc`: the paragraph names `isSignedSelfReply` as it stands, unchanged — the six-hex prefix or the token form with a three-hex tail of either case, nothing after — and the node's ledger row says the same. — Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a disposition before counting the marker**

When a seat writes the bar assessment but omits or mistypes the required `Cured in SHA:`, `Routed to`, or `Rejected` disposition, this explicitly tells todo 1 to accept the marker anyway. For a body-only finding, that comment is the only disposition record, so a below-bar-only round can appear as cure-worthy zero and terminal even though PDR-140's required routing or reasoned rejection was never recorded; require a recognisable disposition field or classify the item as manual.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Below-bar.** Rejected, no write. The disposition PDR-140 requires is the signed reply or comment line itself: the marker is never posted bare — the format says "with the rationale" — and a `Below-bar` line carrying its reasons IS the reasoned rejection, whichever verb it uses (the two recorded replies `3996223154` and `3996223195` are exactly that: rationale, "No write", no verb). Making the count hinge on one of three exact verbs would make the instrument brittle to wording while adding no recorded fact the marker and its rationale do not already carry; the machine counts the marker, the reader reads the rationale, and a line that is only a marker with nothing after it is not a form this contract produces. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a collision-free key for Codex body items**

When one Codex review contains two distinct body findings with the same path, line, and bold heading, both references reduce to the same review ID and item key, so the tally cannot bind a disposition to the intended finding and can mis-deduplicate the count. Fresh evidence in the final text is that the replacement key is the unrestricted bold heading even though no uniqueness constraint exists; use a review-local ordinal or another collision-free identifier as is already done for Copilot items.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Below-bar.** Rejected, no write. The reference already carries the review id, the anchor and the item's heading; the collision needs two distinct Codex findings in one review at one path and line under one identical bold heading, a case no recorded round has produced and the corpus (which has no Codex body item at all) cannot exhibit. The node's mechanism owns deduplication by anchor AND substance, and todo 1 widens the key to an ordinal if that case ever appears; no reader acts wrongly before then (PDR-140 clause 9(a)). Evidence class READ.
